paragraphs.text: Garth (born Galin, nicknamed One-Eye ) was a powerful wizard and planeswalker from Kush on Dominaria .

Garth was a thin man, just over six feet tall, with a bony face, bronzed by the sun, and scruffy, dark hair. Kuthuman described him as "eager, smart, able to use mana almost from the day you were born." He was usually dressed in black and wore a dagger and his spells satchel at his belt. His only arresting features were his eyes, turquoise blue, the left of which he lost when he was young. The lost eye grew back thanks to his ascension , leaving a white star-shaped scar around it. His symbol during the Festival of the Arena was a stylized rendering of an eyepatch. He moved with a deliberate catlike ease, exuding charisma and the sense of mana. When he planeswalked, Garth appeared in a silken black cocoon that spun from a dark line into the size of a human, then split open to reveal the wizard.

Garth was born as Galin, son of Cullinarn , the master of the green-blue House of Oor-tael . The house was destroyed by Kuthuman , the Grand Master of the Arena of Estark , who was on a quest to become a planeswalker . Garth was five years old at the time of the event that would be known as the Night of Fire , and Zarel , the servant of Kuthuman, gouged his left eye out to torment his father. Garth ran back into the burning House and Zarel believed he was dead. In reality, Cullinarn used the last of his power to teleport Garth and his mother far away from the fire. Garth's mother forbade him from seeking revenge, a demand he followed until her death.

Garth spent years hidden away, training and plotting his revenge. After twenty years in exile, he returned to Estark under the false name of Garth and manipulated the remaining houses and the new Grand Master, Zarel, so that he could win the tournament and meet Kuthuman, in what would then be known as the Time of Troubles . During his fights, he became known to the mob as Garth One-eye. He met Hammen , a former servant of Oor-tael, as well as the Benalish soldier Norreen . Garth joined Kestha and later Ingkara , instigating riots in the streets before being captured by the Grand Master 's fighters. He was rescued from prison by Norreen, Hammen, and Varena, a Fentesk fighter with whom he'd had a brief romance. He joined Bolk , whose colors he fought under during the Festival.

In the first round, Zarel rigged the choosing so that Garth was paired with Silmar in a fight to the death, which Garth won. On the second day, Garth won his first two fights easily before fighting the eighth-rank fighter Ulin. Garth was successful in defeating Kuthuman and even managed to somehow use a spell to steal the ability to walk the planes . Later, he willingly gave up planeswalking to live with the Benalish woman known at the time as Norreen, whom he had met during his adventure.

The two retired in the countryside of Gish , with their child Hammen , to grow a vineyard. However, Garth found leaving behind his powers much harder than he had thought, and started journeying between the planes again. It was during one of his absences that Norreen and Hammen were kidnapped and brought to Benalia .

After the death of Sabriam and the rescue of Norreen and Hammen, Garth started a fight with Gull and Greensleeves , thinking they had been the kidnappers. However, Greensleeves quickly brought the wizard to his senses. When confronted by Norreen on his negligence for family duty, Garth admitted the wrongness of his ways, giving up his spells' satchel to Greensleeves and promising he would never abandon his family again. He then offered his knowledge of Dominaria, gathered during his wanderings, in order to bring the people from Gull's army to their homelands. Then he and his family returned to their vineyard, offering their help if Greensleeves requested it.

Garth appeared only in books before Mirage , in which there was no mention of a planeswalker's spark : any mage could break the plane's veil with the right spells and sufficient mana and travel across the planes. To make the content from the early stories fit, many people believe that wizards who became planeswalkers by spells actually possessed sparks that were flared by the spells they cast, but didn't know of these sparks or their role in becoming planeswalkers. However, Garth might be an exception to this theory. The novel Arena states that the spell researched by Kirlen could grant the planeswalking powers to anyone casting it. It's not likely, though, that Kirlen created a real spark with her spell because even planeswalkers don't understand its nature fully. The explanation of this might be that the spell just simulated the powers of Spark to some extent.
In 2021, it was stated in a retcon that Garth's planeswalker spark ignited at the moment he won vengeance against the killer of his kin.
Garth, despite being born to a family and guild of blue-green casters, demonstrated the use of all 5 colors of mana :
White mana: frequently erected Circles of Protection , summoned white knight , Wall of Swords , and Veteran Bodyguards , used Holy Armor , Reverse Damage , and Armageddon .

Blue mana: used Psionic Blast on opponents in the arena. He also used Counterspell s on several occasions, including a Power Sink . Can use Flight on summoned creatures. Summoned a Vesuvan Doppelganger .
Black mana: caught several guards with Terror . Summoned a Drudge Skeleton , Infernal Medusa ; summoned a Lich against Gull .
Red mana: Fireball , Earthbind , Wall of Fire , Wall of Stone , Aerathi Berserker , Rock Hydra .

Green mana: cast Fog , and Stream of Life , summoned Grizzly Bears a war mammoth , Llanowar Elves , Ironroot Treefolk , Wall of Wood , faeries , Wall of Brambles , Giant Growth , Giant Spider , Craw Wurm , and Force of Nature .
Artifacts he possessed: Forcefield , Juggernaut (won from Naru ), Disrupting Scepter , and Living Wall .
